name: Ochraceous-Tawny
lede: Ochraceous-Tawny is a warm, dark orange-yellow, a tawny color pushed toward ochre, and it shares its exact screen color with a second library name, Tawny orange.

sections.title: Tawny, by way of ochre
sections.body: The library files Ochraceous-Tawny from Robert Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature*, plate XV, hue 15 prime, tone i [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 lists give the same swatch's descriptive name as a dark orange yellow [1]. *Ochraceous* means the color of [[ochre]], a family of iron-oxide earth pigments, paired here with *tawny*, the older word for a dark, animal brown-orange [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[dusty-bronze]] and [[dull-orange]], at The nearest distinct neighbor is Dusty bronze, about 2.7 units away by CIEDE2000, [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 61, chroma 48, hue 67 degrees, Munsell 6.7YR 6.0/7.9 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 819 of 23,781 paintings, 3.44 percent, as photographed [2]. It peaks in the 1450s, in 13 of that decade's 109 paintings, about 3.5 times the expected rate [2]. Giovanni Bellini is its most devoted painter here, carrying it in 5 of his 17 works, over 8 times the baseline [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [2].

questions.q: Ochraceous-Tawny shares its exact screen color with which other library name?
